chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: Editing G to T will not produce a reproducible TF-mediated occupancy and regulatory-output change attributable to this base.
The disease association may reflect linkage to another causal variant or a mechanism other than TF binding at this base; the cCRE and gene-level evidence need not identify the causal chain.
POU5F1B need not be a knockout dependency in colorectal cancer cells for a germline risk mechanism to exist.
falsified_if: Isogenic variant editing reproducibly changes TF occupancy and regulatory output, and perturbing the implicated TF removes the allele-dependent effect.

chains.title: Candidate TCF7L2-dependent regulation at the POU5F1B-associated enhancer
chains.element: The variant lies in pELS cCRE EH38E3858447; its target gene is unresolved.
chains.cell_type: HCT116 is a testable context, but the mechanism is not established in primary colorectal tissue.

links.claim: TCF7L2 is occupied over the variant and expressed in HCT116. The ref-favoring QBiC-SELEX result comes from LEF1- and TCF7-mapped models, not a TCF7L2-specific model; it makes ref G a tentative binding direction rather than demonstrating TCF7L2-specific allelic binding.
The variant overlaps the enhancer-like pELS cCRE EH38E3858447, whose target gene is not assigned by the available evidence.
POU5F1B is a candidate target because it is nearby and the T allele is associated with increased POU5F1B expression in transverse colon; neither observation shows that this cCRE mediates that eQTL.
HCT116 is a relevant testing context because TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant is reported there, but this does not establish the mechanism in primary colorectal tissue.

A TCF7L2-to-POU5F1B regulatory effect could contribute to colorectal-cancer susceptibility, but no evidence connects this full chain to the disease association or establishes whether TCF7L2 activates or represses the element.

predictions: An endogenous allele-specific occupancy assay should show greater TCF7L2 occupancy on ref G than alt T if the proposed binding effect is real.
If this chain explains the transverse-colon eQTL, variant editing should make alt T increase POU5F1B expression; a repressive effect of ref-bound TCF7L2 is one possible, unproven explanation.
A reproducible allele-dependent regulatory effect attributed to this chain should be reduced by TCF7L2 perturbation.
falsified_if: A sufficiently powered endogenous assay finds no ref-versus-alt TCF7L2 occupancy difference.
Variant editing produces no reproducible POU5F1B regulatory effect, or TCF7L2 perturbation fails to alter an observed allele-dependent response.

chains.title: Weak alternative: possible SP1-dependent regulation at the candidate enhancer

POU5F1B is a candidate target based on proximity and its positive T-allele transverse-colon eQTL, but mediation by this cCRE is unshown.

An SP1-dependent effect on POU5F1B could contribute to colorectal-cancer susceptibility, but no evidence connects this full regulatory chain to disease or establishes the regulatory direction.

predictions: If SP1 mediates the effect, endogenous assays should find a functionally relevant ref-G versus alt-T difference in SP1 occupancy despite the lack of a clear SP1-specific QBiC-SELEX change.

SP1 perturbation should alter any allele-dependent regulatory response attributed to this chain; a T-associated increase in POU5F1B would require, for example, ref-bound SP1 to repress, which is untested.

SP1 perturbation does not alter a reproducible allele-dependent regulatory response.
